# `get_gain_segment`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return three gain-segment integers from the camera backend.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable (64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb34b0, MIPI backend @0x155620, OpenCamera control-caps loop (64-bit build) |

Reads no parameters. The 64-bit backend writes three integers into the result array: 0, 131, and the camera's maximum for its first SDK control, cached when the camera opens. The first two are fixed in this firmware (READ). Read as [minimum gain, segment break, maximum gain]: that the third is the maximum gain (the SDK lists gain first) is INFERRED. 131 is an imager constant in both builds and in firmware 9.31 and 9.75; the camera libraries switch conversion gain at other points (200 or 80 in the 32-bit build, driver-supplied in the 64-bit build), so whether 131 is a high-conversion-gain switch point on any camera is unresolved (READ). The gain unit is unresolved. Fails with 318 when no camera is open. Firmware 9.31 and 9.75, 64-bit and 32-bit builds (READ): The gain-segment result is `[0,131,max]`, using fixed first and second entries and the cached camera maximum. The value 131 is not calculated from backend conversion-gain parameters. Its physical relationship to a fitted camera's conversion-gain switch remains unresolved.

Side effects: Reads constants and cached gain data into the caller output; no mode change, hardware open or close, or file write in the inspected path. Locks may block; no method-specific timeout. Deeper SDK behaviour is not established.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |

| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_gain_segment"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 318 | Camera is closed (other delegated errors are forwarded from thread-local state; none established) | `device not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"get_gain_segment"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_gain_segment","result":[0,131,400],"code":0,"id":51}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_gain_segment","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":52}
```
